html:
The Sino-British Joint Declaration was signed in Beijing on 19 December 1984 by Margaret Thatcher and the Chinese premier Zhao Ziyang. Britain agreed to hand all of Hong Kong to China on 1 July 1997.

The lease on the New Territories was running out, and Deng Xiaoping refused to extend it. China promised that Hong Kong would keep its capitalist system, laws, freedoms and way of life for fifty years under the formula of one country, two systems, written into the Basic Law of 1990.

Many Hong Kong people feared the future, and after the Tiananmen massacre of 1989 hundreds of thousands emigrated. The handover took place as agreed. Later disputes over elections, the Umbrella Movement and the security law of 2020 turned on whether China had kept its word.
sum: The Sino-British Joint Declaration was signed in Beijing on 19 December 1984 by Margaret Thatcher and the Chinese premier Zhao Ziyang. Britain agreed to hand all of Hong Kong to China on 1 July 1997.
